extracted.intended_audience: federal grant managers, award recipients, auditors, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the OMB Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200) requirements for federal awards, including administrative requirements, cost principles, audit rules, and related compliance guidance for recipients and auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Administrative Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Uniform Guidance establishing a government-wide framework for grants management that synthesizes and supersedes earlier OMB circulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Uniform Guidance provides standard administrative requirements for Federal awards to reduce conflicting guidance and create consistent expectations across agencies (see 2 CFR 200).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies and updates cost reporting guidelines for award recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidance revises cost reporting rules so recipients know how to document and report costs charged to Federal awards; see the full text of the OMB Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200) for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs the focus of audits on areas that have been identified as at risk for waste, fraud and abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits under the Uniform Guidance should prioritize risk areas; auditors should consult the OMB Guidance Compliance Supplements (2017 and 2018) which identify important compliance requirements and modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Conflicting Guidance / Standard Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes previous guidance that is conflicting and establishes standard language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By synthesizing earlier circulars into a single government-wide framework, the Guidance reduces administrative confusion and creates consistent terminology and requirements across Federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance: Reduce Administrative Burden While Guarding Against Waste and Misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The reforms aim to reduce the administrative burden on award recipients and, at the same time, guard against the risk of waste and misuse of Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and implementation decisions under the Guidance should seek this balance — streamlining recipient obligations where possible while maintaining controls to prevent improper use of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize Processing of Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Lays the groundwork for Federal agencies to standardize the processing of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidance encourages standardized data processing across agencies to improve consistency, reporting, and oversight of Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OMB Guidance Compliance Supplements (2017 and 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must use the 2018 Supplement and the 2017 Supplement together; the 2017 Supplement identifies important compliance requirements and the 2018 Supplement modifies sections needing significant revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult both the April 2017 OMB Guidance Compliance Supplement and the May 2018 OMB Guidance Compliance Supplement together when performing audits to ensure application of updated compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and Effective Date (2 CFR 200)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Uniform Guidance is codified at 2 CFR 200 and was implemented with an effective date of December 26, 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to requirements and obligations under the Uniform Guidance should cite 2 CFR 200 and consider the Guidance's effective date for applicability and historical compliance context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Outreach (CFOC Training Webcasts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFOC training webcasts are available to learn about key improvements and changes to grants guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients, auditors, and grant managers should use available training resources (e.g., CFOC webcasts) to understand and implement the Uniform Guidance requirements.
